messages:
alex: Quick heads-up: rolled out a docs + SDK change around sample data sanitization. New policy: all public docs and sample repos must not include real-looking secrets (API keys, tokens, private endpoints). We shipped a pre-commit sanitizer and a CI check in docs-tooling v1.0.0.
pat: ugh good catch. What exactly does the check look for?
sarah: It scans for patterns and entropy heuristics (API key prefixes, jwt-looking strings, aws-style keys) and flags high-confidence hits. It will auto-redact in dry-run mode and block commits in strict mode.
mike: is this enforced automatically for all docs repos?
alex: We enabled dry-run for one week to surface problems, then auto-blocking for PRs touching /docs and /samples in 7 days. We added an allowance workflow for curated exceptions with legal review.
docs-bot: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1255 "policy: sample data sanitization + pre-commit sanitizer". Includes install instructions and CI snippet.
security: Reviewed the scanner - low false positives in internal runs but please treat any flagged string as potentially sensitive. We also added a tip: replace with clearly fake values like API_KEY=REDACTED_EXAMPLE or use the `REDACTED()` helper.
legal: Added template language for contributor docs reminding external contributors not to submit proprietary samples. Also added an exception process for partner-supplied examples that must be staged privately.
pat: paste the pre-commit snippet?
sarah: sure - add to .pre-commit-config.yaml or run manually:```bash
pip install redwood-docs-sanitize==1.0.0
redwood-docs-sanitize scan ./docs --dry-run
# to auto-redact (creates backups):
redwood-docs-sanitize redact ./docs --backup
```
mike: what about CI enforcement? How do teams opt-out during migration?
alex: CI snippet in the PR:```yaml
steps:
  - name: Sanitize docs
    run: |
      pip install redwood-docs-sanitize==1.0.0
      redwood-docs-sanitize scan ./docs || exit 1
env:
  SANITIZE_STRICT: ${SANITIZE_STRICT:-0}
```
pat: timeline for blocking enforcement?
alex: schedule: Day 0 (today) - dry-run mode enabled on all docs repos. Day 7 - enable blocking for PRs touching /docs or /samples. Day 30 - run an org-wide scrub and open PRs to auto-redact historical leaks (with review). Day 90 - require all public samples to include an explicit `SAMPLE_DATA_STATEMENT` frontmatter flag.
security: we'll also trigger an automated notification to security@redwood.ai for any high-confidence findings during the org-wide scrub.
mike: will this affect Dedicated/Private customer repos?
alex: Only public and org-visible sample/docs repos are in scope. Private customer-managed repos are not automatically scanned. We do offer a vendor-runner that customers can opt into to scan their private samples; legal has the docs for that.
legal: partner exceptions: partners can supply redacted examples via a secure upload form. We will not accept unredacted partner secrets in public PRs.
docs-bot: changelog entry added: "docs: sample data sanitization policy and sanitizer tooling v1.0.0; dry-run now, blocking in 7 days; migration guide included."
pat: any migration steps for teams with lots of legacy examples?
sarah: recommended checklist: 1) run `redwood-docs-sanitize scan ./docs --dry-run` 2) run `redwood-docs-sanitize redact ./docs --backup` to apply redactions 3) replace redacted values with `REDACTED_EXAMPLE` or snippet helpers and add `SAMPLE_DATA_STATEMENT` to frontmatter 4) open PRs for review if scrub touched many files.
security: we've queued a small squad to help high-risk teams and will provide a script to automate PR creation for redactions.
alex: we'll post an announcement in #eng-docs and #security with links to the PR and the migration checklist. If anyone needs more time, DM me and we'll grant a short runway. :shield:
legal: one final note - update contributor license and CONTRIBUTING.md to include an explicit statement about not committing secrets. I'll attach sample language to the PR.
docs-bot: docs site updated with policy summary: https://docs.redwood.ai/contributing/sample-data-policy.
mike: thanks all. I'll start running the dry-run on our large SDK samples repo and report back.
